senses.gloss: --the eldest son of Vaivasvata Manu; born of पुत्रेष्टि; anointed by Manu going to Mahendra hill for तपस्; set out for दिग्विजय, when he reached शरवण gardens where उमा was sporting with शिव। There was a curse by which a male who entered the garden was turned into a female. So Ila became इला। Bewildered इला was wan- dering and was met by Budha, Soma's son. She agreed to be his partner and followed him. इक्ष्वाकु and his brothers were concerned at their missing Ila and were told by वसिष्ठ of his whereabouts. On वसिष्ठ's advice, इक्ष्वाकु per- formed an अश्वमेध, as the result of which Ila would be a किम्पुरुष for a month and इला for the next alternately. As इला, she gave birth to पुरूरवस्, the first of the lunar race. In a way Ila was responsible for the two dynasties--solar and lunar. M. ११. ४०-66; १२. 1-१४. [page१-201+ ३०]

(I)--Mother Earth; worshipped for gain of bodily strength.
1: भा. II. 3. 5.
Waited on Hari;
2: Ib. X. ३९. ५५.
saved by Hari in the form of Matsya.
3: Ib. XI. 4. १८.
(II)--one of the wives of Rudra. भा. III. १२. १३.
(III)--the daughter of वायु and one of the queens of Dhruva; her son was Utkala. भा. IV. १०. 2.
(IV)--one of कश्यप's wives. भा. VI. 6. २५, २८; वा. 1. १४१.

(V)--the daughter of Vaivasvata Manu, born of sacrificial ritual in his अश्वमेध। Seeing her father dis- pleased at her birth, वसिष्ठ converted her to a male by name Sudyumna. See इडा; again by शिव's curse he became a woman on whom Budha begot पुरूरवस्; after that she became again Sudyumna. भा. IX. 1. १६, २२; Br. III. ६०. 6; Vi. IV. 1. 9-१३; 6. ३४.
(VI)--the wife of Budha and mother of पुरूरवस्. (See इल). भा. IX. १४. १५; M. २४. 9-१०.
(VII)--one of Vasudeva's wives. Mother of Uru- valka and other sons. भा. IX. २४. ४५ & ४९. [page१-202+ २४]
(VIII)--(इडा): sprang out of a sacrifice of Vaiva- svata Manu in honour of Mitra and वरुण; the latter two adopted her as their daughter. वा. ८५. 7.
(IX)--the wife of Tapas in the विश्वशृज् sacrifice. वा. 2. 6.
--the daughter of तृणबिन्दु. Br. III. 8. ३७; Vi. IV. 1. ४७.
--the नाग with the sun in नभ and नभस्य (आवणि and पुरट्टाशि). वा. ५२. १०.
--a son of अग्नीध्र and apsaras पूर्वचित्ति; lord of इलावृतम् (Sumerumadhyama-वा। प्।) भा. V. 2. १९; Br. II. १४. ४६; वा. ३३. ३९, ४३; Vi. II. 1. १६ and २०.

--the central continent of जम्बू- द्वीप. To its north are mountains नील, श्वेत and शृन्ग- वान्, (सुपार्श्व-वि। प्।) and to its south are निषध, Hema- [page१-203+ ४३] कूट and Himalayas. To its east and west are माल्यवत् and गन्धमादन. (Mandara-वि। प्।). The abode of शिव. He who enters this region would be turned into a woman by the curse of पार्वति. Here शिव worships the Fourth form of विष्णु called सङ्कर्ष्ण by praises.
1: भा. V. १६. 7-१०; १७. १५-24.
इलावृत (s.v.) was its first king.
2: Br. II. १४. ४९; १५. २४, ३३-37.
Here there is no sun or moon; people eat wood apple fruits.
3: Ib. II. १७. 9-१४, २२.
After Ila who spent here the evening of his life; Bali performed यज्ञस् here.
4: M. ११३. १९ & ३०; ११४. ६९; १३५. 2.
Next to हरिवर्ष;
5: वा. ३४. २९.
in shape like a bow and lotus coloured; people here eat of जंबू and live to १३,000 years.
6: वा. ४६. ११-15.
The middle वर्ष of जम्बुद्वीपम् sur- rounding Meru in extent ९००० योजनस्; appears like a ball of smokeless fire; on each of the two sides are three वर्षस् or continents;
7: वा. ३४. २२.
trees special to the region are कदम्ब, जम्बू, पिप्पल, and वट; lies between भद्राश्व and केतुमाल; the forests are चैत्ररथ, गन्धमादन, वैभ्राज and नन्- दन; there are besides four lakes.
8: Vi. II. 2. १५-26.
